business_scope.primary_industry_name: Delivery-Only Multi-Brand Cloud Kitchen Facility Operations

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Title VI (Articles L. 561-1 et seq.) for AML/CFT obligations; Ordonnance n° 2017-563 du 26 avril 2017 relative au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), as amended by Law n° 2021-1754 of 23 December 2021 implementing EU AMLD5

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of Identity and Residence for UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent issuing authority in country of origin (passport, utility bill, or equivalent)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or equivalent for corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry or competent authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against French, EU, UN, and OFAC PEP lists, sanctions lists, and domestic adverse media using certified AML/CFT-compliant tools

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory French language and Latin script; names must adhere to French orthographic rules with no permitted transliteration or foreign characters
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Generic terms implying public services (Postes, Télécommunications, Énergie)
Restricted financial or insurance terminology without prior authorization (Banque, Assurance, Courtage)
Words suggesting state monopoly or public utility
Names identical or confusing with existing trademarks, companies, or public entities
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File administrative appeal with the greffe du tribunal de commerce within two months of rejection notice; subsequent recourse to tribunal administratif if appeal denied

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for SAS entities provided a compliant physical address is designated for correspondence and regulatory filings; ghost-kitchen delivery operations require verification of substance obligations under food-safety and delivery licensing regimes
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium risk (15-25% probability) of unannounced on-site inspections by tax authorities or commercial police during initial two-year compliance period for food-related virtual brands

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Infogreffe or greffe du tribunal de commerce

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media screening services
Registered office address setup and compliance verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Virtual office or corporate address provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for compliant French address meeting statutory requirements

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title II, Chapter VII, Articles L227-1 to L227-20 and R227-1 to R227-2; applicable SAS provisions incorporate specified rules applicable to sociétés anonymes, including Articles L225-3 and L225-5 on capital contributions and fund deposits.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), with registration reviewed by the competent commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce) and recorded in the Registre National des Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online declaration of creation of a legal entity (déclaration de création d'une entreprise) submitted through the INPI Guichet unique, together with the signed SAS articles of association and required supporting documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies; capital may be set at EUR 1 or a higher amount. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years. Funds must be deposited with an authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations, and the deposit certificate must support the filing. The stated USD fee is an approximate conversion of the standard EUR 37.45 commercial registration fee and excludes legal-notice publication and beneficial-owner filing charges.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The President and shareholders resolve that the Company shall accept the subscription of all issued shares in accordance with the signed articles and the subscription schedule, and shall acknowledge receipt of the capital deposit certificate. The registered office is adopted at [full French address] for statutory and administrative purposes. [Name] is appointed President for an indefinite term, with authority to represent the Company in all circumstances permitted by law. [Name] is appointed Directeur Général, if applicable, with the powers specified in the articles. The officers are authorized to complete all registration, tax, banking, licensing, and publication formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate structure and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique; registered-office evidence issued or accepted by the premises provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select the SAS form, confirm the corporate purpose covering delivery-only food preparation and virtual brands, and secure a French registered office. Obtain a lease, domiciliation agreement, or premises occupancy document. Verify that the site permits commercial food preparation and delivery operations under local planning and lease restrictions.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and business purpose
Identification details for shareholders and officers
French corporate tax and contact information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace defective domicile evidence, correct the corporate purpose, or obtain written premises authorization before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute SAS constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders and appointed legal counsel; notarization is generally not required for ordinary cash-capital SAS formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of association in French or with a legally reliable French version. Include the name, form, purpose, registered office, duration, capital, share rights, transfer restrictions, governance rules, President's powers, accounting year, and dissolution provisions. Sign the articles electronically or manually. Use a notarial deed only where a contribution of real estate or another legally protected asset requires it.
required_dossiers: Share subscription and capital allocation schedule
Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend inconsistent articles, obtain missing signatures, and issue a corrected execution version before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized bank, French notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital-deposit account, transfer the subscribed cash contribution, and obtain the certificate of deposit. Ensure the deposited amount matches the articles and subscription schedule. The temporary account is released or converted after registration and delivery of the Kbis extract.
required_dossiers: Executed articles or draft articles accepted by the depositary
Proof of source of funds where requested under AML procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct shareholder or amount discrepancies, provide enhanced source-of-funds evidence, or use another authorized depositary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized French legal-notices publication service (service de presse en ligne or journal d'annonces légales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish an incorporation notice in an authorized medium for the département of the registered office before filing the registration application. The notice must state the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, purpose, duration, President, and registration formalities. Retain the publication certificate.
required_dossiers: President and Directeur Général details, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Republish any notice containing a material error and upload the corrected certificate to the INPI application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic creation declaration, select commercial activity, upload the executed articles and supporting evidence, declare beneficial owners, pay applicable fees, and electronically sign the filing. State the principal activity as delivery-only food preparation and operation of virtual restaurant brands. Keep the acknowledgment and application reference.
required_dossiers: Agent power of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer registry queries through the INPI portal within the stated deadline, upload corrected documents, and pay any additional assessed fee. A refusal may be challenged or resubmitted after curing the stated defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive registration evidence and activate governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial court registry and INPI Registre National des Entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the SIREN, SIRET, APE code, and Kbis extract. Confirm the registered legal representatives and beneficial-owner record. Deliver the Kbis and registration confirmation to the bank to release capital. Maintain the share register, shareholder account records, board or shareholder decisions, and statutory books at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction from the INPI or competent registry for inaccurate identification, address, activity, or officer information.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax, social, food, and local operating registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Service des impôts des entreprises, URSSAF, Direction départementale de la protection des populations, municipality, and other competent local authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm corporate tax and VAT treatment, register as an employer before hiring, file the food-business declaration where required, and complete local premises, signage, waste, and delivery-operational requirements. If alcohol is sold, obtain the applicable licence and complete the required training and municipal declaration.
required_dossiers: Employer and payroll registrations, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to DDPP, URSSAF, tax, or municipal requests; suspend the affected activity until the missing declaration, licence, or corrective measure is completed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction départementale de la protection des populations (DDPP) for food regulation, with the Préfecture and Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL) responsible for applicable environmental and classified-installation matters.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food-business declaration for establishments handling foodstuffs of animal origin (déclaration d'activité relative aux denrées alimentaires d'origine animale), filed with the competent DDPP under Article R233-4 of the French Rural and Maritime Fisheries Code. Approval may be required under Regulation (EC) No 853/2004 if supplying food to other establishments rather than only final consumers.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, acting through the competent regional environmental authority and DREAL; the environmental authority determines screening or assessment requirements.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally no automatic full EIA for a standard urban ghost kitchen. Environmental screening is project-specific under Articles L122-1 and R122-2 of the Environmental Code. An ICPE declaration, registration, or authorization may apply if equipment, storage, combustion, refrigeration, waste, or emissions thresholds are exceeded.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the local sewer authority's discharge authorization or convention, pre-treatment and grease-trap requirements, applicable limits under the Environmental Code and relevant ministerial orders, and lawful waste segregation and traceability. Food waste, used cooking oil, packaging, and hazardous cleaning residues must be collected by authorized channels. VOC, combustion, odor, noise, and atmospheric-emission controls apply where the installed equipment or an ICPE classification triggers them; no universal ghost-kitchen threshold applies without site and equipment data.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal or prefectural fire-safety review where the premises constitute an établissement recevant du public, maintain compliant escape routes, extinguishers, emergency lighting, electrical and gas installations, ventilation, and fire systems, and complete any required accessibility works. Verify structural floor loading for kitchen equipment, extraction systems, cold rooms, and stored goods. Complete occupational-risk assessment documentation, workplace health and safety measures, food-hygiene training, employer registration, and mandatory inspections for relevant lifting, gas, electrical, pressure, or ventilation equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: French Directorate General of Public Finances (Direction générale des finances publiques, DGFiP), through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and, for non-established businesses, the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE). The principal online portal is impots.gouv.fr, supplemented by the formalities portal guichet-unique.entreprises.gouv.fr for business registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is registered through the mandatory business formalities portal, which transmits corporate information to the competent authorities. The DGFiP then allocates the French tax identifiers, including the SIREN, SIRET and VAT identification number where applicable. The French VAT number generally consists of the country prefix FR, a two-character control key and the nine-digit SIREN. A non-established foreign entity carrying out taxable transactions in France must apply for French VAT registration with the SIEE before or promptly after commencing taxable activities, generally by filing the prescribed registration documentation and providing constitutional documents, proof of business activity, identity and authority documents, bank details and, where relevant, evidence of taxable transactions. Businesses established in another EU Member State may use the VAT registration process applicable to non-established EU businesses; businesses established outside the EU may require a French tax representative unless an applicable exemption or mutual-assistance arrangement applies. The VAT number must be verified through the EU VIES system where intra-EU transactions are involved.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) at entity level. A qualifying SAS may elect for income tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu, IR) under Article 239 bis AB of the French Tax Code for a maximum period of five financial years, subject to statutory conditions concerning age, size, ownership, management and business activity. The election is not a US-style check-the-box election and does not generally provide an unrestricted classification choice. France has no general domestic hybrid-mismatch entity election comparable to a check-the-box regime. Anti-hybrid rules may deny deductions or impose inclusion where arrangements produce deduction/non-inclusion or duplicate-deduction outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French value added tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, VAT), forming part of the EU VAT system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The French VAT franchise regime is transaction- and activity-dependent. For ordinary service activities, the principal domestic turnover threshold is generally EUR 37,500, with a tolerance threshold generally of EUR 41,250; for trading and food-service activities, the relevant goods or mixed-activity thresholds are generally EUR 85,000 and EUR 93,500. Thresholds and qualifying categories are subject to statutory annual adjustments and special rules. A ghost-kitchen operator must assess registration based on the actual supplies, including prepared-food sales, delivery charges, platform commissions and any cross-border transactions. Registration may be required voluntarily or immediately under specific intra-EU, import, export, reverse-charge or transaction rules even where a domestic franchise threshold is not exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a universal real-time VAT invoice-clearance system for ordinary domestic business-to-business transactions. Mandatory electronic invoicing will be phased in through approved private platforms and the public invoicing portal under the French reform: all businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; large and mid-sized businesses must issue electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; small and micro-enterprises must issue them from 1 September 2027. Electronic transaction reporting for certain business-to-consumer and cross-border transactions will apply on the same phased timetable. Public-sector invoices are submitted through Chorus Pro. Invoices must contain legally required particulars, be authentic, integral and readable, and be retained for the statutory period. VAT records and transaction data must support audit trails; no general digital stamp or pre-clearance code is presently required for ordinary SAS invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: French VAT is generally not charged on qualifying exports of goods dispatched from France to a destination outside the EU, provided the supplier can prove export and satisfy the applicable invoicing and customs conditions. The exemption is an exemption with right to deduct, rather than a domestic 0% rate. Qualifying intra-EU supplies of goods may be invoiced without French VAT where the customer is VAT-identified in another EU Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State and the supplier satisfies reporting and documentary requirements. Services supplied to a business customer established outside France may be outside the scope of French VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rule; this is technically different from a zero-rated export. Food prepared and delivered by a French ghost kitchen is normally subject to French VAT, commonly 10% for qualifying prepared food for immediate consumption, while alcoholic beverages generally carry 20% and certain packaged food products may qualify for 5.5%. The precise rate depends on product composition, packaging, consumption conditions and delivery model.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration accepted by French Customs (Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects, DGDDI), including the applicable export accompanying or exit confirmation data
Commercial invoice, packing or delivery documentation and transport evidence identifying the goods, supplier, customer and destination outside the EU
Proof of exit from the EU customs territory, such as the electronic exit results, customs-certified export evidence or equivalent carrier and logistics documentation
Bill of lading, air waybill, consignment note or other transport document where applicable
VAT invoice containing the legal reference to the applicable export or intra-EU exemption
For intra-EU supplies, the customer's valid EU VAT identification number, transport evidence and required European Sales List reporting
Bank payment or inward-remittance evidence where commercially available; a French inward-remittance certificate is not a universal statutory prerequisite for every export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline applicable to export VAT relief. Export proceeds remain subject to banking, anti-money-laundering, customs and accounting controls, and sector-specific or contractual requirements may impose separate timing obligations. If the taxpayer cannot substantiate export, transport, customer status or the correct VAT treatment, the DGFiP may reassess output VAT, deny or claw back input-VAT recovery, assess late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month, and impose penalties. A 40% penalty may apply for deliberate failure, while an 80% penalty may apply in cases involving fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights; additional penalties can apply for failure to produce records, inaccurate VAT returns or customs violations. Customs-related breaches may generate separate duties, fines, seizure or other measures under the Union Customs Code and French customs law. Refunds paid on the basis of false, incomplete or unsupported export evidence may be recovered retrospectively, with interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) as monetary and balance-of-payments authority; FX regulatory implementation under the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) and banking supervision by the ACPR (Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current account transactions and capital account transactions, subject to administrative statistical reporting rather than approval. France applies EU capital liberalisation principles; non-EU/EEA capital movements above €10,000 require balance-of-payments declaration via the intermediary bank or direct declaration to DG Trésor. Profit remittance is generally unrestricted but dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are subject to French withholding tax unless reduced by tax treaty, and must be supported by audited financial statements and corporate formalities of the SAS.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or compulsory conversion ratio applies to euro-denominated or foreign-currency export receipts in France. Exporters of services (including restaurant/delivery concept licensing) must repatriate proceeds and may be required to declare foreign assets/receivables for balance-of-payments statistics. There is no statutory timeline for conversion; invoicing can be in any currency, but foreign currency cash balances must be managed under normal banking supervision and reported for prudential/statistical purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for low-risk treasury operations, subject to ACPR e-money institution (EMI) license or passport from another EU/EEA regulator. Legal constraints: EMIs cannot provide lending/credit facilities, and their ability to process certain SWIFT/MT103 cross-border payments may be limited compared to licensed credit institutions. Specifically for a ghost kitchen receiving delivery platform payouts from UberEats/DoorDash, a French EMI account (e.g., Qonto or similar) is viable for SEPA euro settlements but should not be sole banking infrastructure for non-EU vendor payments or escrow balances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML/KYC rules permit fully remote onboarding through video identification and electronic signature under Article R561-5-1 of the French Monetary and Financial Code. However, banks may internally impose face-to-face interview or on-site inspection for non-resident beneficial owners, complex group structures, or when the final beneficial owner is outside the EU/EEA. For a standard SAS with French directors/UBOs, remote opening is generally possible; disloyal refusal by a bank can be escalated to ACPR.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate structure with non-resident shareholders or opaque beneficial owner chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised/legalised register of beneficial owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs), full organisational chart, clear source of funds/wealth statements for UBOs, passports, proof of residency, and up-to-date business plan explaining delivery-only operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High expected turnover with dispersed low-value digital payments and many daily transactions from food delivery platforms
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed contracts with UberEats/DoorDash aggregator platforms, monthly settlement statements, point-of-sale system data export, VAT returns (CA3/CA12), and a documented internal anti-fraud and AML risk assessment aligned with ACPR guidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of capital escrow account or significant incoming injections from abroad for fit-out and brand licensing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder resolution, share subscription agreement, SDK/donation contract, invoice pro-formas from licensors/suppliers, bank account proof from originator bank, and declaration of cross-border capital movement with DG Trésor/Banque de France if above threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mixed commercial activities involving multiple virtual brands under one legal entity (ISIC 5610)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business description and legal opinion that all virtual brands fall under a single operational facility, per-brand cost ledger, trademark licensing agreements, Kbis extrait with correct NAF code, and hygiene/exploitation authorisations from the town hall and prefecture.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer via SEPA Instant Credit or SWIFT MT103 using the SAS's IBAN, with purpose code expressed as 'Apport en compte courant d’associé' (shareholder current account) or 'Augmentation de capital' (capital increase). For non-EU transfers, include the invoice/shareholder agreement reference and ensure the bank files the balance-of-payments declaration to Banque de France. Verification requires the notarised or signed shareholder resolution, Kbis extract, shareholding register, and the injector's own KYC documentation; payments above €10,000 must be traceable and consistent with the entity's profitable ghost kitchen business plan.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For intra-EU supplier payments: SEPA Credit Transfer based on IBAN. For UK/APAC/US brand licensing or equipment imports: SWIFT MT103 with appropriate commodity/service codes, supporting invoices, and customs documents if physical goods are involved. For large capital purchases and recurring royalty payments: Commercial documentary letter of credit opened through a French tier-1 bank, with shipping/verification documents and Incoterms. Food aggregator payouts (UberEats/DoorDash) are settled via automated SEPA transfers into the French operational account; payment rails must be reconciled with daily sales and VAT output.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/GBP and EUR/USD outright forward contracts (ordinary hedging, no speculative purpose)
EUR/USD and EUR/GBP foreign exchange swaps (short-term liquidity management)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (for large, long-term borrowings supporting kitchen facility build-out)
With prior bank risk approval: non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for exotic non-EUR/GBP currencies not routinely deliverable in the French interbank market
Vanilla euro-strike currency options if premium and strike strictly match underlying commercial exposures; exotic barrier options generally not permitted under prudent AML/PRIIPs checks

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (dépôt des comptes annuels) with the Commercial Court Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Infogreffe portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 30 June, subject to court-approved extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers a formal notice, court-ordered compulsory filing with a daily fine (astreinte), criminal fine up to €1,500 (Art. L232-23 Code de commerce), and after repeated default, risk of administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, form 2065-SD and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via impots.gouv.fr
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year financial year, the second working day after 3 May; for other year-ends, within three months after the financial year close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of the corporate tax assessment, 40% if the return is intentionally omitted or fraudulent, plus late-payment interest (intérêt de retard) of 0.20% per month.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner declaration (Déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) confirmation or update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés via Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days of any change in beneficial ownership, including share transfers that alter ownership or control; no separate annual filing when the disclosed information is unchanged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-disclosure or inaccurate disclosure exposes the entity to a criminal fine up to €75,000 for a corporate entity (Art. L561-34 Monetary and Financial Code), plus refusal of Kbis extracts until corrected.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) for an SAS exceeding two of three thresholds as of year-end: total balance sheet €4,000,000; net turnover €8,000,000; average employee headcount 50. Audit also becomes compulsory when the entity controls or is controlled by a company meeting the thresholds or pursuant to a court decision requested by shareholders holding at least 10% of capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général); IFRS is permitted for consolidated financial statements of listed groups and voluntary for unlisted groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under French law there is no autonomous annual UBO filing; the RCS beneficial-owner declaration must be updated within 15 days of any change of ownership or control arising from share transfers. During the annual accounts filing process the legal representative certifies the continuing accuracy of the beneficial-owner data. Any inconsistency prevents the issuance of a compliant Kbis extract and triggers criminal liability.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of Directors and Resolutions (registre des procès-verbaux du directoire)
Minute Book of Shareholders Decisions (registre des décisions et assemblées générales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $300–$800 per year for a registered office address and corporate agent services in France
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,500–$10,000 per audit engagement where a statutory auditor is required or voluntarily appointed

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). Qualifying small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to statutory conditions, including turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% ownership by individuals or qualifying entities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: France generally has no broad corporate tax holiday for an SAS. Qualifying SMEs may use the 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit. Eligible research and development expenditure may qualify for the research tax credit, generally at 30% of eligible expenditure incurred in metropolitan France up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold, subject to statutory conditions. Other potentially relevant incentives include regional investment regimes, employer social contribution reliefs, and tax credits for specified activities. Tax losses are generally carried forward without a fixed expiration period, subject to the annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the current year's taxable profit; loss carryback is generally limited to the preceding financial year and capped by the lower of the preceding year's profit and EUR 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return), filed electronically through the French tax administration's professional online account on impots.gouv.fr using EFI, or through an authorized EDI provider. Supporting schedules generally include forms 2058-A-SD, 2058-B-SD, 2058-C-SD, 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD, and applicable balance-sheet, income-statement, and tax reconciliation schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; corporate income tax instalments are generally paid quarterly.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on a date other than 31 December, the return and tax payment are generally due within three months after year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the return is generally due by the second business day following 1 May of the following year. Four corporate income tax instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, with a final balance payment generally due by the return deadline. Newly formed companies and companies with low prior-year liability may qualify for instalment exemptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, tax office, financial year dates, legal form as Société par Actions Simplifiée, and whether the return is original, amended, or filed following a cessation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French SAS as the taxable entity. Identify the foreign shareholder or parent only where requested by ownership, group, related-party, or tax-consolidation schedules. A foreign shareholder does not eliminate the French company's domestic filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss after reconciliation of accounting income with French tax rules, including non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax credits, provisions, depreciation adjustments, and limitation regimes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include income and expenses attributable to the French SAS. Do not deduct foreign-head-office costs, royalties, interest, or management charges unless they are genuine, documented, arm's-length, properly allocated, and supported by transfer-pricing evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductions converting accounting result into taxable result, including non-deductible taxes, excess depreciation, provisions, penalties, gifts, entertainment, related-party adjustments, and tax-exempt items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile intercompany charges, platform fees, brand costs, financing expenses, and foreign exchange items separately. Maintain invoices, contracts, benefit evidence, allocation keys, and payment records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year tax loss, carried-forward losses utilized, remaining losses, and any loss carryback claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the annual loss utilization cap. Track losses by year and preserve evidence supporting their origin. A change in activity, merger, or significant restructuring can restrict or forfeit loss utilization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax basis, acquisitions, disposals, depreciation, amortization, exceptional depreciation, and capital gains or losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify kitchen equipment, leasehold improvements, software, trademarks, and delivery-related assets under French tax depreciation rules. Distinguish deductible operating expenditure from capital expenditure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base, applicable rate, gross tax, credits, instalments, foreign tax credits where available, and final balance or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% standard rate unless a documented preferential rate applies. Treaty relief normally affects withholding taxes rather than the French SAS's own corporate tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information concerning controlled transactions, foreign related parties, tax consolidation, and transfer-pricing documentation where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose transactions with non-French group companies, including brand royalties, management services, procurement, financing, platform arrangements, and cost recharges. Ensure consistency with statutory transfer-pricing files and any country-by-country reporting obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research tax credit, audiovisual or cultural credits, apprenticeship or other eligible credits, and related supporting schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits supported by French eligibility requirements, contemporaneous cost records, employee or project evidence, and any required declarations. Foreign development work is not automatically eligible for a French credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Value-added tax contribution declarations and settlement, subject to turnover thresholds and applicable legislative rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assess French establishment, turnover, payroll, and local value-added thresholds separately from corporate income tax. Confirm current-year exemption or phase-out rules before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Foreign related-party and country-by-country reporting schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual country-by-country report notification and, for qualifying French ultimate parents or reporting entities, country-by-country report filing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SAS belonging to a foreign group must identify the reporting entity and jurisdiction where required. The French entity may have a notification obligation even when the report is filed abroad.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing generally triggers a 10% surcharge, increased penalties for formal notices or persistent non-compliance, and late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month. Deliberate evasion may trigger a 40% penalty; fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of rights may trigger an 80% penalty. Understatement, unsupported deductions, inaccurate transfer-pricing positions, and failure to produce required documentation may generate tax reassessments, interest, specific transfer-pricing penalties, and joint or several liability procedures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2572-SD for corporate income tax balance payment, generally submitted electronically through the professional account on impots.gouv.fr or through EDI.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual balance payment, with quarterly instalments made during the financial year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The balance is generally due by the deadline applicable to the annual corporate income tax return. Instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, legal name, tax office, financial year, and payment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS's own SIREN and tax account. Do not use the foreign parent's tax identification number as the primary taxpayer identifier.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax calculated for the relevant financial year after credits and adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tie the amount to form 2065-SD and preserve a reconciliation to the statutory accounts and tax computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax instalments already paid, refundable credits, and amounts withheld or otherwise creditable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify payment references, bank debits, and credit eligibility. Do not treat foreign withholding taxes as French instalments unless a specific French credit mechanism applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net amount payable or refund claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the payment account is authorized for the French tax account and that refund claims are supported by the relevant tax-credit documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment generally generates 0.20% monthly interest and may generate a 5% late-payment surcharge in addition to filing-related penalties. Incorrect or missing payment references can delay allocation and create apparent arrears.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident are generally subject to a 25% withholding tax for corporate recipients, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. Dividends paid to individuals are generally subject to a 12.8% withholding tax, subject to statutory exceptions. A qualifying EU parent may obtain exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive implementation where ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. Payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions may be subject to substantially higher rates.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Confirm the recipient's treaty residence, beneficial ownership, legal form, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test exposure, minimum participation conditions, and holding period. Obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's competent tax authority and retain ownership and anti-abuse evidence. Where French administrative procedure permits relief at source, provide the required treaty forms or certificates to the French payer before payment. Otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and file a refund claim with the French tax administration using the applicable form and supporting tax-residence, payment, ownership, and beneficial-ownership evidence. Treaty rates vary by treaty and dividend ownership percentage.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties and similar payments to non-residents are generally subject to a domestic withholding tax of 25%, subject to treaty relief, EU interest-and-royalties exemptions, beneficial-ownership conditions, and anti-abuse rules. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, except for specified anti-abuse, non-cooperative-jurisdiction, or special-category situations; payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions can be subject to a 75% rate. Treaty rates commonly reduce royalty withholding to approximately 0% to 10% and interest withholding to 0% to 10%, but the exact rate depends on the applicable treaty, recipient status, beneficial ownership, and payment characterization.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million threshold. Full transfer-pricing documentation, including a Local File and Master File, is generally mandatory for French entities or French tax groups meeting the statutory turnover or gross-assets threshold, or belonging to a group meeting the applicable threshold. Smaller entities remain subject to the arm's-length principle and must be able to substantiate related-party pricing. French transfer-pricing documentation and reporting requirements have been strengthened for financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2024. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups meeting the EUR 750 million consolidated revenue threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a single, separately branded Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Substance is nevertheless required under French anti-abuse principles, beneficial-ownership rules, the general anti-abuse rule, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, withholding-tax provisions, and treaty principal-purpose-test standards. A French SAS should maintain genuine local management, decision-making, personnel or operational capacity proportionate to its functions, premises or documented access to operating infrastructure, books and records, commercial risk assumption, and evidence of services received. A conduit company, artificial royalty owner, circular-financing vehicle, or entity lacking decision-making capacity may lose treaty benefits and face reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing turnover, fabricating expenses, understating taxable profit, falsifying invoices, operating undeclared delivery activity, or submitting materially false tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late interest, 40% penalty for deliberate conduct, or 80% penalty for fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of rights. Criminal tax fraud may carry up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine; aggravated cases may carry up to seven years' imprisonment and a EUR 3 million fine, subject to statutory aggravating conditions. Corporate criminal fines may be multiplied under the Penal Code, with confiscation and commercial prohibitions also possible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face criminal prosecution, personal fines, imprisonment, confiscation, management bans, and civil liability. Tax authorities may seek joint and several liability under Article L267 of the French Tax Procedures Code where a manager's fraudulent conduct or repeated serious non-compliance makes tax collection impossible. Travel restrictions are not an automatic tax penalty but may arise from judicial control, arrest warrants, or criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT fraud and fictitious input-tax recovery
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register or report French VAT, claiming input VAT on fictitious invoices, misclassifying restaurant and platform transactions, manipulating delivery-platform settlement statements, or using false intra-EU supplies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, interest, 40% or 80% penalties depending on conduct, potential loss of VAT rights, and criminal prosecution for fraud or document falsification. Additional penalties may apply for failure to issue compliant invoices or retain required records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed to criminal fines, imprisonment, management bans, and tax-enforcement liability where they knowingly organized or tolerated VAT fraud. Insolvency proceedings may generate claims for insufficiency of assets if management misconduct contributed to the shortfall.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive brand royalties, management fees, procurement charges, platform fees, or shareholder interest; shifting French kitchen profits to a low-tax affiliate without functions, assets, or risks; or failing to support pricing with contemporaneous analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm's-length adjustment, corporate tax, withholding tax, interest, penalties, and specific documentation-related penalties. Failure to produce required documentation can trigger a penalty generally equal to the greater of the statutory minimum and a percentage of reassessed profits, subject to legal caps and current-law calculation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability where transactions are knowingly abusive, fictitious, or detrimental to the French company. Deliberate concealment can escalate to tax-fraud prosecution; ordinary documentation failure does not automatically create imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, treaty abuse, or beneficial-ownership failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SAS as a conduit to receive dividends, royalties, or interest for a foreign party while lacking operational substance, disguising the beneficial owner, or routing payments through entities established principally to obtain treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or domestic exemptions, withholding-tax reassessment, interest, 40% or 80% penalties, general anti-abuse reassessment, and potential criminal consequences if documents or declarations are falsified.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for intentional misrepresentation, abuse of corporate assets, tax fraud, or participation in money laundering. Corporate separateness generally remains effective for legitimate liabilities, but fraudulent or abusive conduct can support personal and insolvency-related claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold or remit tax on cross-border payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, salaries, or other French-source income to non-residents without applying the correct withholding, relying on an unverified tax-residence certificate, or failing to file withholding returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid withholding tax from the French payer, interest, filing penalties, and possible penalties for deliberate concealment or abuse. Treaty relief may be denied if residence, beneficial ownership, or procedural evidence is deficient.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The company is ordinarily the primary debtor. Directors may incur personal or criminal exposure where non-withholding was deliberate, repeated, fraudulent, or connected with insolvency or asset stripping.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining incomplete books, suppressing cash or delivery revenue, issuing non-compliant invoices, destroying accounting records, or failing to reconcile Uber Eats, DoorDash, payment processors, and bank receipts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment based on estimated turnover, rejection of deductions, penalties, accounting sanctions, and possible criminal liability for false accounting or document destruction. French accounting and tax records generally require long-term retention, commonly ten years for accounting documents, subject to the applicable record category.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil, criminal, and insolvency liability for organized concealment, fictitious accounting, or destruction of evidence. A court may impose management bans or order restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained cash, failing to identify beneficial owners, ignoring suspicious payment flows, making unexplained related-party transfers, or failing to maintain required customer and supplier due diligence where AML obligations apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory measures may include warnings, injunctions, administrative fines, business restrictions, asset freezing, and criminal prosecution for money laundering. Money laundering can carry imprisonment and substantial fines, with aggravated penalties for organized or repeated conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be prosecuted as principals or accessories, face imprisonment, fines, confiscation, management bans, and civil restitution. Travel restrictions may be imposed by judicial authorities in criminal proceedings but are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful distribution, asset stripping, or insolvency misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable profits, paying shareholder or affiliate amounts while insolvent, preferring related creditors, transferring assets below value, or continuing operations while unable to meet liabilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unlawful distributions, repayment claims, clawback of transactions, insolvency proceedings, director liability for insufficiency of assets, and possible bankruptcy-related criminal sanctions including misuse of corporate assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to contribute personally to the company's liabilities, disqualified from management, fined, or imprisoned in serious cases. The corporate veil is not automatically pierced; liability normally requires statutory grounds, personal misconduct, fraud, or insolvency-related fault.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using undeclared kitchen staff, misclassifying employees as contractors, omitting tips or benefits, failing to operate payroll withholding, or concealing labor supplied through related entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Back-payment of social contributions and payroll taxes, reassessments, surcharges, labor penalties, exclusion from public benefits, and criminal penalties for travail dissimulé, potentially including imprisonment and significant fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president or de facto manager may face personal criminal liability, management bans, imprisonment, and civil claims for employee entitlements and social-security losses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a ghost kitchen without required food-registration, hygiene, municipal, alcohol, waste, fire-safety, or commercial permits; concealing allergens; or breaching cold-chain and traceability rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative closure, withdrawal or suspension of authorization, product seizure or destruction, fines, civil claims, and criminal penalties for public-health or consumer-protection offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability for knowing or negligent breaches, particularly where unsafe food causes injury. Insurance coverage may be denied for intentional or grossly negligent conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating undisclosed virtual brands, misleading consumers about restaurant identity or origin, using fake reviews, concealing surcharges, misrepresenting allergens, or manipulating platform rankings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Injunctions, administrative fines, consumer refunds, damages, platform suspension, and criminal penalties for deceptive commercial practices, with aggravated sanctions in specified circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally prosecuted where they authorized or knowingly maintained deceptive practices. Civil liability may extend to consumer losses and regulatory remediation costs.
